- **self**: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms (7/5)

## How it works

- [statement] Because Ollama pulls weights under upstream licenses, a pulled model is not automatically free for commercial or redistributed use: check the model's license blob for user-count gates, attribution, naming and acceptable-use clauses before shipping or redistributing. (medium confidence) — https://dev.meta.ai/llama/llama4/license/ · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ollama's Terms of Service (last updated May 2026) do not mention a model library, third-party model licenses, or redistribution of models; they cover lawful use, output verification, user content and indemnity, and disclaim third-party services. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/terms · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://ollama.com/library/llama3.2/blobs/fcc5a6bec9da
- [statement] Each Ollama library model exposes its upstream license text as a blob; the llama3.2 blob shows the Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement (version date 2024-09-25), so the upstream license, not an Ollama license, governs the weights. (medium confidence) — https://ollama.com/library/llama3.2/blobs/fcc5a6bec9da · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://ollama.com/terms
- [statement] Llama 4 Community License (effective 2025-04-05): products with more than 700M monthly active users in the prior month must request a license from Meta, which may refuse; distributors must display 'Built with Llama'; models created, trained, fine-tuned or improved using Llama materials or outputs must have names starting with 'Llama'; use must follow the Acceptable Use Policy. (high confidence) — https://dev.meta.ai/llama/llama4/license/ · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://opensource.org/?p=121585
- [statement] Gemma Terms of Use (last modified 2026-04-01) apply to Gemma 1-3: Gemma Prohibited Use Policy incorporated by reference, Google reserves the right to restrict usage 'remotely or otherwise', redistribution of Gemma or Model Derivatives (including distilled/synthetic-data-trained models) requires passing on use restrictions and a copy of the terms; Google claims no rights in outputs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-01) — https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://opensource.googleblog.com/2026/03/gemma-4-expanding-the-gemmaverse-with-apache-20.html
- [statement] Gemma 4 ships under the OSI-approved Apache 2.0 license (Google open source blog, 2026-04-02), described as the first Gemma family release under Apache 2.0; the Gemma terms page points Gemma 4 to a separate Apache 2.0 license. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-02) — https://opensource.googleblog.com/2026/03/gemma-4-expanding-the-gemmaverse-with-apache-20.html · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms
- [statement] OSI's Open Source AI Definition 1.0 requires freedoms to use, study, modify and share, plus data information, complete training/run code and parameters under OSI-approved terms. The OSI states Llama 3.x is 'still not Open Source by any stretch of the imagination' (2025-02-18), citing field-of-use limits, user discrimination, and an EU exclusion; so 'open-weight' is the accurate label for Llama. (high confidence) — https://opensource.org/ai/open-source-ai-definition · keywords: Open-weight model licenses and Ollama library terms · also: https://opensource.org/?p=121585
